title: The Milkmaid and Her Pail

full_text:
Patty, the milkmaid, had filled her polished wooden pail with rich, creamy milk from the morning milking. Balancing the heavy pail gracefully upon her head, she set off down the sunny country lane toward the market town, her mind drifting into delightful daydreams of future fortune.

"The milk in this pail will easily sell for three silver coins," she reasoned with a bright smile. "With three silver coins, I shall purchase a hundred eggs from farmer Giles. Even if some are addled, at least eighty plump, healthy chicks will hatch in the spring.

"I will feed the chicks on grain and kitchen crumbs until autumn, when fat pullets bring the highest price at the Michaelmas fair. With the money from my poultry, I will buy a stunning silk party dress of emerald green, with ribbons of crimson and slippers of fine leather.

"I will wear this dazzling gown to the Christmas ball! All the handsome young men will flock around me, begging for a dance. The miller's son will ask for my hand, and the wealthy farmer's boy will plead for a smile. But I shall toss my head with haughty disdain and say: 'No!'"

Lost in the intoxication of her daydream, Patty suited the action to the thought: she gave her head a sharp, proud toss!

Instantly, the wooden pail slipped from her head and crashed onto the stony lane. The fresh, creamy milk poured out into the dirt, soaking into the dry dust until not a single drop remained!

Weeping bitterly over the white puddle, Patty returned home to face her mother's scolding, learning the eternal truth that building castles in the air without watching your feet brings present ruin.
moral: Do not count your chickens before they are hatched; keep your mind on the task at hand.
